The feeder number is a quasi-identifier that, combined with substation, pinpoints a specific geographic zone in the power distribution network. In the context of power grid data, a specific feeder serves a defined set of consumers, making it a location-based identifier that can narrow down to a small group of individuals. Under GDPR principles, this constitutes a location identifier that can be used to re-identify individuals when combined with consumption data.

The substation identifier is a geographic location identifier that, combined with the feeder number, uniquely identifies a specific area in the power grid. This is analogous to a physical address or geographic location that can be used to identify a group of individuals residing in or connected to that area. Location data is classified as tracking data in the DPV ontology, indicating higher privacy sensitivity.

The date field provides temporal precision that, when combined with feeder and substation identifiers, creates a specific spatiotemporal reference point. This allows tracking of consumption patterns over time for a specific area, which constitutes historical tracking data. Temporal identifiers are quasi-identifiers that increase re-identification risk when combined with other location-based data.
